currentCourseInput.title: Amplifying Perceived Value Techniques
currentCourseInput.body:
# M082 · Amplifying Perceived Value Techniques

**Practices · Emotional · Practice / tool**

Source status: Recovered manuscript

> The explanation follows the cited sources. Examples, practice questions and application guidance are authored for this expansion unless identified as source material. Illustrations are not observed outcomes.

## 1. See it

You are absorbed in repetitive corrections and no longer notice who benefits when the explanation becomes usable.

## 2. What it is

A way to reconnect a pursuit with its core value, concrete effects, wider contribution or actual progress when that value has become hard to see.

## 3. Why it exists

It restores a view of what the work genuinely enables, rather than demanding enthusiasm by force.

## 4. First principles and mechanism

Attention can narrow to immediate cost. Relevant examples or actual progress can restore omitted value, but cannot make an ineffective activity valuable by rhetoric.

## 5. When to use it

**Use:** Use when the pursuit’s value is supported but temporarily obscured.

**Do not use it this way:** Do not fabricate impact, manipulate yourself with grandiose claims or retain a pursuit whose value has genuinely disappeared.

**What you need:** Concrete outcomes, beneficiaries or progress that are actually supported.

## 6. How to use it

Source-informed application guidance. Where the source supplies a sequence, its meaning is retained; additional setup, examples and checks are instructional expansion, not newly attributed original doctrine. Original wording is available in the source panel.

1. Name the core value.
2. Inspect concrete effects and any wider contribution.
3. Review real progress and what remains unresolved.
4. Decide whether the restored view justifies continuing or whether the arrangement still needs change.

## 7. Watch it happen

Illustration: an instructor sees a learner independently use the corrected method. That observation can make the tedious revision’s purpose visible. A projected claim of helping millions cannot substitute for the actual result.

**Comparison or near miss:** Reducing unnecessary difficulty may be more useful than highlighting value when the value is already clear.

## 8. Now you do it

**Try it now:** Find one actual effect that explains why the work matters.

**Guided question:** Is an inspiring hypothetical outcome enough to claim the work already has that value?

**Model answer:** No. Keep possibility and achieved contribution separate.

**Independent transfer:** Apply the practice to maintaining a useful result, not only creating something new.

## 9. How you know

**Learner check:** You can reconnect to value without inflating claims.

**Outcome check:** The clearer view supports a justified action or a justified decision to change.

**What would change the account:** If the claimed benefit is contradicted by actual use, revise the pursuit.

## 10. Connect and multiply

- **supports [Value > Suffering](M070.md)** — Clarifies the value side.
- **uses [Agency / Meaningful Capability Expansion (MCE)](A04.md)** — Asks what capability matters to the recipient.
- **requires [Fact or cap](M021.md)** — Checks impact claims.

## 11. Original sources and revisions

**Manuscript locator:** p. 43 (82-page source edition).

**[S01] Manuscript — 82-page edition.** Supplied manuscript; authorship/adoption of every wording is not independently established. File: `sources/Manuscript.pdf`.

Expansion edition: 2026-10-24. These teaching materials have been source-checked and structurally inspected; independent learner effectiveness has not been measured in this production run.
